children: Food delivery platform Zomato has introduced a separate fee of up to Rs 30 on cash-on-delivery orders, with the charge varying across users and order values, according to media reports.

Listed as a “Pay on Delivery Fee” in the order bill, the charge is levied when customers choose to pay for their orders in cash at the time of delivery. The fee is separate from Zomato’s existing platform fee and other applicable charges.

The amount is not uniform across orders. Different fees were displayed for orders of varying values, though the exact basis for calculating the charge, including whether it is linked to order value, location or other factors, could not be immediately ascertained, PTI reported.

Zomato’s latest charge comes as food delivery platforms increasingly explore additional fee structures and monetisation avenues to improve profitability. The company already levies a platform fee on food orders, along with applicable delivery, packaging and other charges.

The development comes amid a broader focus among food delivery companies on improving unit economics and monetising different aspects of the customer ordering experience. While convenience and platform fees have become increasingly common, companies have also been experimenting with new charges and pricing models as they seek to strengthen margins.
